cap: A seminiferous tubule has two compartments. Spermatogonia sit in the basal compartment on the basement membrane, and the tight junctions between Sertoli cells, the blood-testis barrier, shield the meiotic cells and spermatids above them from the immune system. FSH acts on the Sertoli cells inside the tubule, while LH acts on the Leydig cells in the interstitium outside it, which is why the two pituitary hormones control sperm support and testosterone separately.
teach: Read the figure from left to right as a germ cell's journey: it starts as a spermatogonium outside the barrier, crosses the Sertoli tight junctions as a committed cell, completes meiosis I and II in the adluminal compartment, remodels during spermiogenesis, and is released into the lumen still unable to swim. A breach of the tight junctions (vasectomy, trauma, torsion, mumps) exposes the adluminal antigens and produces antisperm antibodies.
